items.title: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam
items.description: Nearly eight years after Epic took on Steam with its own Game Store and launcher, the Fortnite maker is deploying a new tool to give it an edge over Valve: vibe coding. In announcing the new publicly available "Preview" build of its Epic Games Launcher, Epic writes that "programming is hard. So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look." And while that might sound a little tongue-in-cheek, Epic Games Store General Manager and VP Martin Keely told PC Gamer that the team "started from scratch" and used AI as "a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously." The goal, Keely said, was to "look at functionality that existed [in the current Epic Games Launcher] and [say] we want to replicate that, but not the code itself." Speaking to IGN , Keely clarified that using AI to code the new Launcher "made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well." items.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
items.description: A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment. Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases. Cutting proteins The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid. This is critical for building up the long chains found in proteins. (The amino acids also have side chains with distinctive chemistry, which gives a backbone specific properties.) items.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
items.description: It took OpenAI two days to notice that a recording device was hidden in a restricted executive conference room where leadership met to discuss highly confidential information, including technical progress, government engagements, and commercial partnerships. Only those with special clearance are supposed to access that room. But the FBI believes the recording device was planted by Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer from Saudi Arabia, who became a permanent US legal resident in 2020. In a press release Tuesday announcing his arrest, the FBI alleged that chatbot logs and CCTV footage suggested that Alfozan—who worked as an OpenAI engineer for more than a year—sought to use the device to spy on OpenAI and risked leaking trade secrets in a way that threatened national security. To conceal the USB device, Alfozan allegedly wrapped it in toilet paper, then plugged it into the back of a conference room television. The device was likely planted on September 28, and OpenAI found it on September 30 and quickly determined that its contents were encrypted, the FBI said. Days later, on October 5, OpenAI installed a camera in that conference room, and the CCTV footage allegedly showed Alfozan attempting to retrieve the recording device that same day. items.title: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary.
items.description: AI is mass decompiling games. That's both awesome and scary. Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly). I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development: Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to any software. [...] This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[ With console makers going all in on digital and games becoming entirely unplayable due to servers shutting down, this is fantastic news. We could own software we bought regardless of what the company thinks. Via Hacker News Tags: computer-history , game-design , ai , webassembly , generative-ai , llms , ai-ethics , coding-agents

items.title: Build self-improving document processing using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.description: IDC research shows that document-related challenges cost organizations $19,732 for each information worker annually and reduce productivity by 21.3 percent. Organizations receiving invoices from hundreds of suppliers often face layouts that vary by issuer and change without notice. Template-based systems require constant maintenance at this scale. Staff can spend up to 30 percent of their time on document-related tasks, and manual data entry error rates range from 1–4 percent . Conventional intelligent document processing (IDP) solutions address some of this burden, but they require extensive upfront configuration for each document format and break when layouts vary across vendors. In this post, you learn how to build an agentic IDP system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that classifies, extracts, validates, and learns from business documents with minimal human intervention. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Your agents automatically handle new document formats, such as supplier invoices, purchase orders, insurance claims, and loan applications. By the end of this post, you can: Deploy a multi-agent IDP system, often in under 20 minutes. Process new document types without manual template configuration. Let agents train themselves on each new document format and reuse what they learn, so later documents of that type go straight to extraction without retraining. Challenges with rule-based document processing Many IDP pipelines require you to define templates, extraction rules, and validation logic for every document format upfront. When a new vendor sends a purchase order with a different layout, the pipeline breaks. This creates three core challenges: Template rigidity: Each new document format requires manual configuration, and even minor layout changes can cause extraction failures. No learning: The same extraction errors repeat across similar documents because the system doesn’t retain knowledge from previous corrections. Scaling burden: Each new vendor or document variant multiplies the maintenance effort, and organizations processing documents from hundreds of sources face ongoing operational costs. An agentic approach addresses these challenges. Instead of static templates, AI agents analyze each document, generate extraction instructions, validate results, and learn from corrections automatically. Over time, your system builds a knowledge base of document formats, so you process similar documents with minimal additional configuration. Solution overview In this solution, eight specialized agents collaborate across two graph-based workflows running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The following diagram shows the multi-agent workflow graph built using Strands Agents , an open source SDK for building AI agents. Figure 1: Multi-agent orchestration workflow graph Identification workflow : The Analyzer agent extracts text using Amazon Textract and identifies the document type and sender. The Matcher agent searches for similar documents using vector similarity in Amazon S3 Vectors , a capability of Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). Training workflow (new document types): When no match is found, the Instructions agent generates extraction prompts, the Extractor agent extracts structured data, and the Validator agent checks results against schemas and business rules in Amazon Aurora DSQL . If validation fails, the Instructions Fixer agent refines the prompts and retries. On success, the Save Instructions agent persists the instructions for reuse. Automation workflow (known document types): When a match is found, the Extractor agent uses existing instructions. If validation fails, the Troubleshooter agent fixes the extracted data directly without modifying instructions. How it works The following diagram shows the infrastructure architecture for the solution. Figure 2: Agentic IDP infrastructure architecture on AWS Business documents arrive in Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) or direct upload to Amazon S3. Amazon EventBridge triggers an AWS Lambda function that creates a tracking job in Amazon DynamoDB and invokes AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. AgentCore runtime orchestrates document processing through Strands Agents. Your agents securely access AWS resources through machine-to-machine credentials managed by AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Cognito . Your Lambda functions become agent-compatible tools through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface of AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Agents extract text using Amazon Textract, classify documents using vector embeddings in S3 Vectors, and validate data against business rules in Aurora DSQL. Agents access enterprise data through MCP servers to validate extracted content against business rules. You monitor status and troubleshoot issues through a chat-enabled dashboard hosted on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). You gain visibility into agent performance through AgentCore Observability, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon CloudWatch telemetry. Deploy the solution Follow these steps to deploy the solution infrastructure and web UI to your AWS account. Prerequisites To deploy this solution, you must have: An AWS account . Access to Amazon Bedrock with Amazon Nova and Anthropic (Claude) models enabled. For model availability by AWS Region, refer to Supported models by AWS Region in Amazon Bedrock . Access to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore (Runtime, Gateway, Identity), S3 Vectors, and Amazon Aurora DSQL in a supported Region . AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) v2 installed. Docker installed and running (required for building and deploying container images). Python 3.11+ and Node.js 18+. items.title: Generate presentations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.description: A financial services team spends significant time each week manually creating client PowerPoint presentations from quarterly reports, compliance documents, and market analyses. Each presentation requires reading hundreds of pages, extracting key data points, structuring slides, and generating supporting visuals. This post walks you through building an AI agent system using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that automates this workflow, completing in under 90 seconds in our internal testing. This approach reduces presentation creation time while grounding content in source documents. The solution deploys a supervisor agent on AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, using the Strands Agents framework to orchestrate document generation and summarization tools. Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 (available on Amazon Bedrock) handles content creation, Amazon Titan Text Embeddings v2 powers vector search, and Stability AI Stable Image Inpaint (available on Amazon Bedrock) generates slide images. This post includes a public repository with the code assets. Solution overview The solution deploys a single supervisor agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime that selects between document generation and summarization tools based on user requests. A Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline uses Amazon OpenSearch Serverless for vector storage and semantic search across multimodal content. The solution includes a REST API built with .NET 8 minimal APIs, so you can integrate with existing enterprise applications through standard HTTP calls. AWS Lambda offers serverless compute, including containerized functions for PowerPoint generation. The solution secures the implementation with Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) isolation, AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption, and AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) least-privilege access control. Key concepts This section covers AgentCore runtime, RAG, and content safety guardrails as they apply to this solution. Agent orchestration with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore A single AI agent generating documents from large knowledge bases must retrieve content, structure outlines, generate text, create images, and assemble files. Rather than implementing these competing responsibilities in a monolithic function, the solution uses a tool-based architecture where a supervisor agent routes requests to specialized tools. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime provides a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. The agent code runs in an isolated container with session management, built-in identity, and observability. The solution uses the Strands Agents framework (an open source SDK for building AI agents) to implement the supervisor logic. The supervisor agent exposes two tools: generate_pptx: Creates PowerPoint presentations by invoking the PPTX Generator Lambda function, which retrieves content from the knowledge base, generates slide outlines, creates AI images, and assembles the final document. generate_summary: Extracts and synthesizes information from the knowledge base using RAG to deliver accurate, grounded responses. The agent determines whether a request requires document generation, content summarization, or both, then invokes the appropriate tool. You can add new capabilities by defining new tools in the agent code without modifying existing ones. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) for enterprise knowledge RAG addresses a fundamental challenge in AI systems: delivering accurate, up-to-date information grounded in enterprise data rather than relying solely on the model’s training data. The implementation uses Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases , which combine vector search with large language models (LLMs) to retrieve relevant context before generating responses. The RAG pipeline works as follows: You upload enterprise documents to Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) . The system chunks and parses documents, applying special handling for multimodal content including tables, charts, and images. Amazon Titan Text Embeddings v2 converts each chunk into high-dimensional vectors that capture semantic meaning. Amazon OpenSearch Serverless stores the vectors, creating a searchable vector database. At query time, the system converts the user’s request into an embedding and performs similarity search to retrieve relevant document chunks. Retrieved chunks supply context to the language model, which generates responses grounded in the source material. This approach is designed to help reduce hallucinated content by grounding generated documents in source information from the enterprise knowledge base. Note: The Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection data plane must remain publicly accessible because Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases accesses Amazon OpenSearch Serverless from AWS-managed infrastructure, not through customer VPC endpoints. IAM data access policies protect the collection, and VPC-only access restricts the Amazon OpenSearch Serverless dashboard. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails for content safety Enterprise AI applications require content moderation to meet organizational standards and compliance requirements. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails offers built-in content filtering and safety mechanisms integrated throughout the document generation pipeline. Guardrails operate at multiple stages: Input processing: Filters user requests to help prevent injection issues and inappropriate content. Output generation: Monitors model outputs to verify compliance with content policies. Personally identifiable information (PII) handling: Detects and anonymizes or blocks PII. The implementation creates custom guardrails through AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) , configured with specific policies tailored to enterprise document creation. The agent applies guardrails at the model invocation level, providing consistent content safety without requiring manual configuration for each deployment. Solution architecture The fol

items.title: How Tamnoon built AI-powered cloud security remediation with Amazon Bedrock
items.description: Critical cloud exposures pile up faster than security teams can close them. Cloud-native application protection platforms (CNAPP), cloud providers, and posture scanners generate more findings than any team can triage, and risk accumulates in the gap between detected and fixed. Most findings sit untouched, not because they’re hard to fix. Someone must investigate context, identify the owner, confirm the fix won’t break production, and then do it at a volume that outpaces headcount. In this post, we share how Tamnoon built Tami, an agentic cloud remediation orchestrator on Amazon Bedrock , to close that gap. Tami autonomously investigates findings ingested from CNAPP and cloud-native sources and assesses whether remediation is safe. It then generates and orchestrates the fix with guardrails and governance wherever a change touches a customer’s cloud. The approach drove an over 90 percent reduction in critical cloud exposure in 90 days with zero production issues. About Tamnoon Tamnoon is an AI-powered cloud security remediation platform that works alongside CNAPPs. Its AI assistant, Tami, helps human cloud security experts investigate, prioritize, and safely remediate misconfigurations and issues across customer environments in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and other cloud providers. Tamnoon integrates with the CNAPPs and cloud-native tools teams already use and turns their findings into validated, production-safe fixes. Most of the work including investigation, prioritization, and remediation planning happens before anything touches a live environment, which is what makes automated remediation trustworthy at scale. Cloud security remediation challenges A security engineer can spend hours investigating a single finding. Often, it traces back to the same root cause as dozens of other alerts. Alert volume overwhelms headcount: CNAPPs and scanners generate thousands of findings. Teams can’t triage them all, so critical exposures sit unresolved while risk compounds for months. Investigation is manual and repetitive: Each finding requires context gathering on who owns the resource, what depends on it, whether the fix is safe. This eats hours of senior engineer time, repeated across every item in the backlog. Fear of production impact blocks automation: Teams hesitate to automate remediation because they can’t risk taking down production. Without confidence that a fix is safe, nothing moves. Reactive prioritization: Without a way to cluster related findings or score remediation confidence, teams work through alerts linearly rather than addressing root causes that resolve many issues at once. Tamnoon’s solution addresses the full pipeline from finding ingestion to validated fix. The platform treats these challenges as interconnected rather than isolated problems. Solution overview Tamnoon takes you from initial finding to executing the fix. The platform ingests findings from CNAPP, Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) providers, and other security tools and normalizes them into a unified schema. It then enriches them with asset and exposure context and prioritizes them. From there, the agentic layer takes over using a set of specialized AI agents, each running in an event-driven, serverless architecture on AWS, so every stage scales independently and fails safely. Agentic architecture on Amazon Bedrock The platform delegates work to four specialized agents, each responsible for a distinct phase of the remediation pipeline: An investigation agent draws on training from millions of real customer cloud environments to determine context, filters that context through a large language model (LLM)-as-a-judge validation layer. It reasons through the remediation goal, operational scope, and cloud-provider-specific verification, producing read-only investigation steps and a complete investigation plan. A safety-scoring agent builds an evidence chain per asset, combining automated verification results with analyst findings. It classifies each finding’s remediation as SAFE, RISKY, or AWAITING DATA with a deliberately conservative bias. When in doubt, it downgrades. A remediation agent activates only for findings that the safety agent has deemed safe. It reasons through ordering, dependencies, and conditions, then produces a remediation plan in which every step follows a backup, remediate, and verify structure and includes rollback guidance. A code-generation agent turns plan steps into executable remediation, but only after an input guardrail screens for relevance and prompt injection. Every artifact passes an automated generate-and-review loop in which a separate reviewer agent must approve the output. Why Amazon Bedrock When the Tamnoon team set out to build Tami, the choice of foundation model (FM) platform was going to shape everything that followed. Tamnoon’s remediation agents don’t all do the same kind of work. Some perform deep investigative reasoning to understand the root cause of a security finding. Others handle high-volume validation, checking proposed fixes quickly and cheaply. Still others review generated code, balancing quality against cost on every task. Matching each of these jobs to the right model, without stitching together a different integration for each one, was a core requirement. That requirement is what made Amazon Bedrock the natural fit. Through a single API, each agent can call the foundation model best suited to its task. The most capable models handle the hardest reasoning. More efficient models take on the repetitive, high-throughput work. Review-focused models optimize the trade-off between output quality and cost. items.description: Choosing the right model for a specific application requires a practical way to test it with representative inputs. Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides access to a broad catalog of already pretrained models. In this post, we show how to deploy an available model from SageMaker JumpStart, run a lightweight and repeatable performance test using the SageMaker Python SDK, and delete the endpoint when testing is complete. For supported models and available capacity, this workflow provides a repeatable evaluation path, although deployment time varies by model, instance type, quota, and AWS Region. In 2026, SageMaker JumpStart introduced two improvements that simplify model discovery and deployment. In the Model Hub section of the Amazon SageMaker AI console, you can browse the SageMaker JumpStart catalog, view sample notebooks, and open them directly in SageMaker Studio. Additionally, you can now go from Hugging Face model discovery to SageMaker AI deployment in a single click using the new deep link integration. Solution overview Our approach uses a reusable Python script that performs three steps: Discover and deploy a model from SageMaker JumpStart. items.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
items.description: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results do raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms. Challenging to shut down Anthropic further warned not only about the new potential malware, but also that it could be difficult to stop. In its blog post, it wrote that “a replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own.” Read full article Comments

items.title: AIエージェントを自作する方法7選！無料で始める手順と費用の目安
items.description: AIエージェントは、GeminiやClaudeの画面で指示文を登録するだけでも自作できます。本記事では、 難易度別の7つの自作方法 と、同じニュース要約エージェントを3通りの方法で作る手順を解説します。 「AIエージェントを自作して情報収集を自動化した」という投稿を見て、自分も作りたいと考えたことはないでしょうか。いざ調べると、Difyやn8n、Pythonなど選択肢が多すぎて手が止まりがちです。 自作の成否は、自分のスキルに合う方法を選べるかで決まります。いきなりコードから始めると環境構築でつまずき、逆に指示文だけで済ませると定時実行のような自動化に手が届きません。 本記事では、指示型・連携型・自律型の3段階に分けた自作方法と、「毎朝の業界ニュース要約エージェント」を各段階で作り比べる手順を中心に紹介します。 読み終えるころには、 自分が最初に作るエージェントと、その作り方 が決まっています。まずは7つの方法の違いから確認していきましょう。 AIエージェントを自作する方法は難易度別に7つ AIエージェントを自作する方法は、難易度の低い順に以下の7つです。 【指示型】Geminiのスキル 【指示型】ClaudeのProjects 【連携型】Dify 【連携型】n8n 【自律型】Claude Code 【自律型】PythonとAgents SDK 【自律型】OllamaとローカルLLM 段階 方法 できること 必要なスキル 費用 指示型 Geminiのスキル ClaudeのProjects 決まった手順の作業を、呼び出すたびに同じ品質でこなす プログラミング不要 無料から 連携型 Dify n8n 決まった時刻に動き、外部サービスから情報を集めて通知する プログラミング不要 無料から 自律型 Claude Code PythonとAgents SDK OllamaとローカルLLM 使える道具を自分で選び、手順を考えながら作業を進める コードを読める程度 有料プランやAPI利用料がかかる場合あり 自分が任せたい作業に最も近い段階から選ぶと、遠回りせずに最初の1体を完成させられます。 【指示型】Geminiのスキル Geminiのスキルは、よく使う作業手順を登録しておき、チャットで「/」を入力して呼び出せる機能です。 Google AIの有料プランに入っていなくても使えます 。 作成方法は4つあります。Geminiと会話しながら作る方法、テンプレートを編集する方法、空のテンプレートに手で書く方法、SKILL.mdファイルを読み込む方法です。 ただし、利用できるのは18歳以上の個人Googleアカウントのみで、仕事用・学校用アカウントには現時点で対応していません。従来のGemsは、個人アカウントでは2026年11月からスキルへ自動移行されます。 参考： Gem からスキルへの移行について（Gemini アプリ ヘルプ） プログラミングに触れたことがない人が、最初の1体を作るのに向いています。 出典： Gemini アプリのスキルを作成、管理する（Gemini アプリ ヘルプ） 【指示型】ClaudeのProjects ClaudeのProjectsは、指示文と参考資料をまとめて登録し、その前提でClaudeと会話できる機能です。 無料プランでも5つまで作れます 。 過去の企画書や社内用語集、文章の書き方ルールなどをナレッジとして読み込ませておけば、毎回説明し直す手間がなくなります。たとえば「自社トーンで報告書を下書きする担当」のような使い方に向いています。 なお、資料が多いときに容量を最大10倍まで広げる機能（RAG）は、ProやMaxなどの有料プラン限定です。 手元の資料を読ませて仕事をさせたい人に向いています。 出典： What are projects?（Claude Help Center） 【連携型】Dify Dify（ディフィ）は、ブロックを線でつなぐ操作でAIアプリを組み立てられるオープンソースの開発基盤です。 社内資料を検索して答えるチャットボット のように、資料とAIを組み合わせる用途に強みがあります。 クラウド版の無料プラン（Sandbox）では、200回分のメッセージクレジットとアプリ5つまでの枠が用意されています。手元のPCやサーバーにDockerで立ち上げるセルフホストも可能です。 作ったアプリはWebページとして公開できるため、家族やチームに使ってもらう場面でも役立ちます。 資料を参照するAIを、画面操作だけで作りたい人に向いています。 出典： Pricing（Dify） 【連携型】n8n n8n（エヌエイトエヌ）は、Gmail・Slack・Googleスプレッドシートなどのサービスをつないで作業を自動化するツールです。 「毎朝9時に実行する」といった定時実行 を簡単に設定できます。 AI Agentノードを使うと、AIが状況に応じて道具を選びながら作業を進める仕組みも組めます。指示型ではできない「人が呼び出さなくても動く」エージェントを作れる点が特徴です。 ライセンスキーなしで動かすセルフホスト版は無料のCommunity Editionとして使えます。サーバー管理をしたくない場合は、有料のクラウド版を選べます。 決まった時刻に情報を集めて届けるような、繰り返し作業を任せたい人に向いています。 出典： Self-hosting n8n（n8n Docs） 【自律型】Claude Code Claude Codeは、ファイルの読み書きやコマンドの実行まで自分で進めるAnthropic社のAIエージェントです。 「こういうエージェントがほしい」と日本語で伝えるだけで、コードを書いて動かすところまで任せられます 。 自分でコードを書けなくても、Claude Codeに作らせたコードを読みながら修正を頼む形で開発を進められます。後述するPythonのエージェントも、Claude Codeに作らせると短時間で形になります。 ただし、無料プランでは使えません。Pro以上のサブスクリプションか、API利用料を前払いするClaude Consoleのアカウントが必要です。 コードは書けないものの、本格的なエージェントを作りたい人に向いています。 出典： クイックスタート（Claude Code Docs） 【自律型】PythonとAgents SDK PythonでAIエージェントを自作する場合は、OpenAIのAgents SDKのような開発用ライブラリを使うのが近道です。 エージェントが道具を選んで実行する繰り返し処理を、ライブラリが肩代わりしてくれます 。 自分で書くのは、エージェントへの指示文と、エージェントに使わせる道具（Pythonの関数）だけです。ほかにも、Claude向けのClaude Agent SDKや、Gemini向けのADK（Agent Development Kit）があります。 費用はAPIの従量課金が中心で、使った分だけ支払う形です。 エージェントが動く仕組みを理解し、細かく作り込みたい人に向いています。 出典： Quickstart（OpenAI Agents SDK） 【自律型】OllamaとローカルLLM Ollama（オラマ）は、手元のPCでLLM（大規模言語モデル）を動かすための無料ツールです。 データを外部のAIサービスに送らずにエージェントを動かせます 。 OllamaはMITライセンスのオープンソースで、ツール呼び出し（関数呼び出し）にも対応しています。Pythonから呼び出せば、クラウドのAPIを使わない自作エージェントを組めます。 ただし、動かせるモデルの大きさはPCのメモリやGPUの性能で決まります。クラウドの最新モデルと比べると、回答の精度は下がると考えておきましょう。 API利用料をかけずに試したい人や、個人のメモなど外に出したくないデータを扱いたい人に向いています。 出典： Tool calling（Ollama） AIエージェントを自作する前に決める4つのこと AIエージェントの自作に取りかかる前に、以下の4つを決めておきます。 任せる作業を1つに絞る AIと人の担当範囲を分ける 入力と出力の形を決める 成功の基準を決める ここが曖昧なまま作り始めると、完成したのに使わないエージェントが残るだけになります。 任せる作業を1つに絞る 最初のエージェントには、 毎日または毎週くり返している作業を1つだけ 任せます。 「情報収集と資料作成とメール返信をまとめて任せたい」と欲張ると、指示文が長くなり、どこで失敗したのかを特定できなくなります。作業を1つに絞れば、うまくいかないときの原因を探しやすくなります。 たとえば「毎朝15分かけている業界ニュースのチェック」のように、所要時間と頻度を言える作業が候補です。 1つの作業で成果を実感できれば、次に任せる作業も自然と見えてきます。 AIと人の担当範囲を分ける 作業の流れを分解し、 AIに任せる部分と人が確認する部分 を先に決めておきます。 AIは事実と異なる内容をもっともらしく出力することがあります。とくにメールの送信やファイルの削除など、取り消せない操作をAIだけで完結させると、間違いがそのまま外に出てしまいます。 ニュース要約なら「記事の収集と要約はAI、社内に共有するかの判断は人」のように線を引きます。 担当範囲が決まっていれば、どの段階でどの方法を使うべきかも判断しやすくなります。 入力と出力の形を決める エージェントに 何を渡し、どんな形で返してほしいか を具体的に書き出します。 入力と出力が決まっていないと、実行するたびに結果の形式がばらつき、結局は人が整え直すことになります。 ニュース要約なら、入力は「RSSで取得した記事のタイトルとURL」、出力は「重要な3件を各100字で要約し、URLを添えた箇条書き」のように決めます。 出力の形まで決めておけば、そのままSlackやメールに流せる結果が返ってきます。 成功の基準を決める 作ったエージェントが役に立っているかを判断するため、 数字で測れる基準 を1つ決めておきます。 基準がないと「なんとなく便利」のまま改善が止まり、気づけば使わなくなります。 たとえば「ニュースチェックの時間が15分から3分に減る」「要約の手直しが週1回以下になる」といった基準です。最初から完璧を求めず、基準を満たすまで指示文を直していきます。 基準を満たしたかどうかで、次の段階の方法へ進むかも判断できます。 【指示型】Geminiのスキルでニュース要約エージェントを自作する手順 Geminiのスキルを使えば、以下の4ステップで、プログラミングなしでニュース要約エージェントを作れます。 ステップ1：作業手順を指示文に書き出す ステップ2：スキルの作成画面を開く ステップ3：名前・実行内容・指示を入力する ステップ4：「/」で呼び出して指示文を直す このあと紹介するn8nやPythonでも同じ題材を扱うため、方法ごとの違いを比べられます。 ステップ1：作業手順を指示文に書き出す 最初に、自分がふだん手作業でしているニュースチェックの流れを、 Geminiへの指示文として書き出します 。 スキルの精度は指示文の具体性で決まります。「いい感じにまとめて」ではなく、対象・件数・形式まで書くことが大切です。 あなたは生成AI業界のニュース担当です。 以下の手順で作業してください。 1. 直近24時間に公開された生成AI関連のニュースを検索する 2. 企業の新サービス発表、大型の資金調達、法規制の動きを優先して3件選ぶ 3. 各ニュースを100字以内で要約し、出典URLを添える 4. 最後に「自社の業務に関係しそうな点」を1行で添える 出力は箇条書きにしてください。確認できない情報は書かないでください。 このように手順を番号で区切っておくと、Geminiが作業を飛ばさず進めてくれます。 ステップ2：スキルの作成画面を開く パソコンでは、以下の操作で スキルの作成画面 を開きます。 gemini.google.comにアクセスする サイドバーの「カスタマイズ」をクリックする（見当たらない場合は「その他」から開く） 上部の「スキル」をクリックする 「作成」から「手動で作成」を選ぶ スキルを使うには、Geminiの「アクティビティの保存」をオンにしておく必要があります。また、機能は段階的に提供されているため、アカウントによってはまだ表示されない場合があります。 「Geminiで作成」を選ぶと、会話しながらスキルを作ることもできます。 参考： Gemini アプリのスキルを作成、管理する（Gemini アプリ ヘルプ） ステップ3：名前・実行内容・指示を入力する 作成画面では、 名前・実行内容・従うべき指示 の3つを入力し、上部の「作成」をクリックします。 名前：呼び出すときに使うため、「ai-news-digest」のように短くする 実行内容：「生成AI関連の最新ニュースを3件選んで要約する」のように1文で書く 従うべき指示：ステップ1で書き出した指示文を貼り付ける 実行内容の文は、Geminiが会話の流れから自動でスキルを使うときの判断材料になります。何をするスキルなのかが一読で伝わるように書きましょう。 作成したスキルは「スキル」ページに保存され、あとから何度でも編集できます。 ステップ4：「/」で呼び出して指示文を直す チャット欄で「/」を入力し、作成したスキルを選んで実行します。 結果を見ながら指示文を直す ことで精度が上がります。 items.title: AIエージェントの作り方を初心者向けに解説！Geminiで無料作成する5ステップ
items.description: AIエージェントを作ってみたいものの、解説記事を読むとDifyやPythonの話ばかりで、何から手をつければよいかわからない方は多いのではないでしょうか。 初心者がAIエージェントを作るなら、 普段使っているGeminiの「スキル」機能から始めるのが最短ルート です。無料で使え、指示文を入力するだけで完成するため、プログラミングの知識はいりません。 一方で、2026年はChatGPTのGPTsが廃止予定となり、GeminiのGemsもスキルへの移行が決まりました。古い解説記事のとおりに作ると、作り直しになるおそれがあります。 本記事では、Geminiで最初の1体を作る5ステップと、初心者でも精度が出る指示文の型を中心に解説しています。 読み終える頃には、 自分専用のAIエージェントが1体動いている状態 になっているでしょう。まずは初心者に合うツールから確認していきましょう。 初心者におすすめのAIエージェント作成ツール4選 初心者がプログラミングなしでAIエージェントを作れるツールは、以下の4つです。 Gemini：スキルで作る Copilot：Agent Builderで作る Claude：プロジェクトで作る ChatGPT：個人プランでは新規作成できない ツール 無料で作れるか 必要なアカウント 向いている人 Gemini 作れる 個人のGoogleアカウント まず1体作ってみたい人 Copilot Web検索を使うエージェントなら作れる 職場のMicrosoftアカウント Microsoft 365を使う職場の人 Claude 5つまで作れる Claudeのアカウント 資料を読ませて使いたい人 ChatGPT 個人プランでは作れない Business以上の法人契約 法人契約がある職場の人 ※2026年10月時点の各公式サイトの情報 自分の利用環境に合わないツールを選ぶと、アカウントの準備だけで手が止まってしまいます。 Gemini：スキルで作る 初心者に最もおすすめなのが、 Geminiの「スキル」機能 です。 スキルは、役割や手順を書いた指示文を保存しておき、チャット欄から呼び出して使う機能です。Googleの有料プランに加入していなくても作れます。 利用条件は、18歳以上の個人Googleアカウントで「アクティビティの保存」がオンになっていることです。普段Geminiを使っている方なら、追加の準備はほとんどいりません。 参考： Gemini アプリでスキルを作成、使用する（Google） 本記事の実践パートでは、このスキルを使って最初の1体を作ります。 Copilot：Agent Builderで作る 職場でMicrosoft 365を使っているなら、 Microsoft 365 Copilotの「Agent Builder」 が候補になります。 Copilotの画面で「New agent」を選び、名前や指示を入力して作ります。Copilotのライセンスがなくても、Web情報を根拠に回答するエージェントであれば無料で作れます。 社内のSharePointやメールを参照させる場合は、ライセンスか従量課金が必要です。また、モバイルアプリでは作成できない点にも注意しましょう。 参考： Choose between Agent Builder and Copilot Studio（Microsoft） Claude：プロジェクトで作る Claudeでは、 「プロジェクト」に指示と資料を固定すると、特定の作業専用のAIエージェント として使えます。 サイドバーの「Projects」から新規作成し、「Set project instructions」に指示を入力します。参照させたいファイルは、画面右側のナレッジ欄から追加します。 無料プランでも5つまで作れるため、マニュアルや資料を読ませて質問に答えさせる使い方を試したい方に向いています。 参考： How can I create and manage projects（Anthropic） ChatGPT：個人プランでは新規作成できない ChatGPTでは、 個人プランで新しいGPTsを作ることはできません 。 Free・Go・Plus・Proの個人アカウントは、作成済みのGPTを使うことはできるものの、新規の作成・公開はできなくなっています。さらにOpenAIは、カスタムGPTを2026年12月11日に廃止する予定と案内しています。 参考： Creating and editing GPTs（OpenAI） 参考： Custom GPT retirement and migration FAQ（OpenAI） 「GPTsで作る」と紹介している古い記事も多いため、これから始める初心者は GeminiかClaudeを選ぶと作り直しを避けられます 。 【実践】GeminiでAIエージェントを作る5ステップ GeminiでAIエージェントを作る手順は、以下の5ステップです。ここでは例として、会議メモからタスクを抜き出すエージェントを作ります。 任せたい作業を1つ決める 指示文を書く スキルを作成する 「/」で呼び出してテストする 結果を見て指示文を直す 所要時間は30分ほどで、終わる頃には毎日使える自分専用のAIエージェントが完成します。 ステップ1：任せたい作業を1つ決める 最初に、 AIエージェントに任せる作業を1つだけ 決めます。 「メールも議事録も資料作成も」と欲張ると、指示文が長くなり、どの作業も中途半端な出力になるためです。 選んだ作業は、「何を渡すと、何をして、何を返すか」の3つに分解します。今回の例では以下のとおりです。 渡すもの：会議のメモや文字起こし すること：決定事項とタスクを抜き出す 返すもの：担当者と期限付きのタスク一覧 ここまで決まれば、次のステップで書く指示文の骨組みはできあがっています。 ステップ2：指示文を書く 次に、ステップ1の内容をもとに指示文を書きます。 役割・手順・出力形式・わからない時の対応の4要素 を入れるのがポイントです。 あなたは会議の内容を整理するアシスタントです。 貼り付けられた会議メモを読み、以下の手順で整理してください。 1. 決定事項を箇条書きで抜き出す 2. タスクを抜き出し、担当者と期限を整理する 3. 次回までに話し合う論点をまとめる 出力は「決定事項」「タスク一覧（表形式）」「次回の論点」の順にしてください。 担当者や期限がメモに書かれていない場合は「未定」と記載し、推測で補わないでください。 指示文は、メモ帳などにテキストで保存しておきましょう。後から修正するときや、別のツールで作り直すときにそのまま使えます。4要素の詳しい書き方は、次の見出しで解説します。 ステップ3：スキルを作成する 指示文ができたら、Geminiでスキルを作成します。操作は以下のとおりです。 Geminiのメニューから「カスタマイズ」を開く 「スキル」ページに移動し、「手動で作成」を選ぶ 名前に「会議タスク整理」、実行内容に「会議メモからタスクを抜き出す」と入力する 指示の欄にステップ2の指示文を貼り付け、「作成」を押す 名前は、 後から呼び出すときに思い出しやすい短い言葉 にしておくと便利です。 指示文を自分で書くのが難しい場合は、「Geminiで作成」を選ぶと、対話しながら指示文を作ってもらえます。テンプレートから作る方法もあるため、慣れないうちは試してみましょう。 ステップ4：「/」で呼び出してテストする 作成したスキルは、 チャット欄で「/」に続けてスキル名を入力すると呼び出せます 。 呼び出したら、過去の会議メモを貼り付けて動作を確かめます。テストに使うメモは、以下のように条件を変えて3〜5件用意しておくと、苦手なパターンを見つけやすくなります。 担当者と期限がすべて書かれているメモ 担当者や期限が抜けているメモ 雑談が多く、決定事項が少ないメモ 社外秘の情報を含むメモは使わず、 個人で作ったダミーのメモや公開済みの情報 でテストしましょう。 ステップ5：結果を見て指示文を直す テストの結果が期待どおりでなければ、 うまくいかなかった点を指示文にルールとして追記 します。 AIエージェントの精度は、最初の指示文ではなく、修正の回数で上がっていくためです。 たとえば、雑談の内容までタスクとして抜き出してしまった場合は、「確定した依頼だけをタスクとし、検討中の話題は含めない」と1行追加します。修正はスキルの編集画面から行い、同じテスト用メモで再確認します。 3〜5件のテストで期待どおりの結果が出たら完成です。毎日の業務で使いながら、気づいた点を少しずつ足していきましょう。 初心者でも精度が出る指示文の4要素 AIエージェントの精度を左右する指示文には、以下の4要素を入れます。 役割を決める 手順を番号で書く 出力形式を指定する わからない時の対応を決める この型を覚えておけば、どのツールで作る場合も指示文で迷わなくなります。 役割を決める 指示文の冒頭では、 AIエージェントが誰として振る舞うかを1文で宣言 します。 役割が決まると、AIは言葉づかいや判断の基準をその立場に合わせて出力するためです。 悪い例：メールを書いてください。 良い例：あなたは法人営業の担当者です。取引先に送る丁寧なビジネスメールを作成してください。 役割に業種や相手を含めるほど、手直しの少ない出力が得られます。 手順を番号で書く 作業の進め方は、 「1.」「2.」のように番号付きで順番に書き ます。 文章でまとめて指示すると、AIが手順を飛ばしたり順番を入れ替えたりすることがあるためです。 悪い例：内容を読んで要約して、大事なところをまとめてください。 良い例： 1. 文章を読み、主張を1文で要約する 2. 根拠となる事実を3つ抜き出す 3. 自社の業務への影響を1文で書く 手順を分けておけば、うまくいかない時に どの手順を直せばよいか がすぐにわかります。 出力形式を指定する 結果の形は、 表・箇条書き・文字数などで具体的に指定 します。 形式を決めないと、同じ指示でも毎回違う形で返ってきて、そのままコピーして使えないためです。 悪い例：わかりやすくまとめてください。 良い例：「項目」「内容」「担当者」の3列の表にまとめ、各セルは30字以内にしてください。 出力形式がそろえば、日報やチャットへの貼り付けなど次の作業にそのままつなげられます。 わからない時の対応を決める 最後に、 情報が足りない時にどう返すかを指示 しておきます。 指示がないと、AIは足りない部分をもっともらしい内容で補ってしまい、誤った情報が混ざる原因になるためです。 悪い例：（とくに指示しない） 良い例：資料に書かれていない内容は「記載なし」と答え、推測で補わないでください。 この1文があるだけで、出力を確認する手間が大きく減り、安心して業務に使えるようになります。 初心者が最初に作りたいAIエージェントの例5選 初心者が最初に作るなら、以下の5つがおすすめです。 議事録を要約するエージェント メール返信の下書きを作るエージェント ニュースを集めて要約するエージェント 日報を作成するエージェント 資格学習をサポートするエージェント 指示文の例をそのまま貼り付ければ、すぐに試せます。 議事録を要約するエージェント 会議の文字起こしを渡すと、 要点を短くまとめた議事録 を作るエージェントです。 元の文字起こしと見比べれば正しく要約できたかをすぐに確認できるため、最初の1体に向いています。 あなたは議事録の作成担当です。 貼り付けられた会議の文字起こしを読み、以下の形式で議事録を作成してください。 ・会議の目的：1文 ・話し合った内容：箇条書きで5件以内 ・決定事項：箇条書き 文字起こしに書かれていない内容は推測で補わないでください。 メール返信の下書きを作るエージェント 受け取ったメールを渡すと、 返信の下書きを敬語で作成 するエージェントです。 返信の方針だけを自分で伝えれば、文面を考える時間を減らせます。 あなたは法人営業の担当者です。 貼り付けられたメールへの返信文を作成してください。 1. 相手の用件を1文で整理する 2. 私が指定した方針（承諾・辞退・確認など）に沿って返信文を書く 3. 丁寧なビジネス敬語で、300字以内にまとめる 方針が指定されていない場合は、返信文を書かずに方針を質問してください。 送信前には、宛名や日付などの事実関係を 必ず自分の目で確認 しましょう。 ニュースを集めて要約するエージェント 指定したテーマのニュースを検索し、 重要な順に要約して一覧にする エージェントです。 Web検索を使うため、社内の資料を用意しなくても成果を実感できます。 あなたは業界ニュースのリサーチ担当です。 私が指定したテーマについて、直近1週間のニュースを検索してまとめてください。 ・重要度の高い順に5件 ・各ニュースの要約は100字以内 ・各ニュースの出典URLを必ず記載する 出典URLを出させておけば、気になったニュースの元記事をすぐに確認できます。 日報を作成するエージェント その日の作業メモを渡すと、 決まった型の日報に整える エージェントです。 箇条書きの走り書きでも、提出できる形に整えてくれるため、毎日の作業時間を短縮できます。 あなたは日報の作成アシスタントです。 貼り付けられた作業メモを、以下の形式の日報に整えてください。 【本日の業務】箇条書き 【成果・進捗】箇条書き 【課題と明日の予定】箇条書き メモにない成果や予定は書き足さないでください。 資格学習をサポートするエージェント 学びたい単元を伝えると、 要点の解説と確認問題を出してくれる エージェントです。 業務データを使わないため、個人のアカウントでも気兼ねなく試せます。 あなたは資格試験の学習コーチです。 私が指定した単元について、以下の手順で学習を支援してください。 1. 単元の要点を5つの箇条書きで説明する 2. 理解度を確かめる4択問題を3問出す 3. 私の回答を採点し、間違えた問題を解説する スキルとして保存しておけば、 毎回同じ流れで学習を進められる ため、学習の習慣化にも役立ちます。 作ったAIエージェントを育てる3つのコツ 作ったAIエー

items.title: OpenAI, Google pushing new AI models easily tricked into making nudes, researchers say
items.description: Safety researchers continue to warn that a large volume of AI-generated explicit content is spreading unchecked, while regulators do little to meaningfully stop it. This non-consensual content is commonly shared in text and direct messages or stored in private clouds where it’s less likely to be detected or reported, a Google co-authored study of Internet users across the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom found this July. That’s why the “most critical intervention point” remains at the source: the harmful AI tools used to make the fake sexual images, Google researchers concluded. Yet red-teaming in recent months suggests that as some of the leading AI image generators from Google and OpenAI become more capable, they may be getting worse at blocking explicit outputs. Read full article Comments

NVIDIA is putting that principle into practice, including through a five-year, $250 million compute commitment to strengthen the U.K.’s agentic safety and security research. NVIDIA’s Investments in the UK NVIDIA has been investing in the U.K. startup ecosystem, supporting companies including Basecamp Research , Ineffable Intelligence , Synthesia , Wayve and many more. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Boltz , Foresight , Hiverge, Prima Mente and Riverlane . Boltz , a London-based AI startup founded by MIT researchers, builds biomolecular models and AI agents that help scientists predict molecular structures and interactions, and design potential new medicines. Foresight, a London-based startup, helps owners of major infrastructure projects, including hyperscale data centers, predict completion dates, mitigate risks and accelerate time to revenue. Hiverge , a Cambridge-based AI startup founded by researchers from Google DeepMind and the University of Cambridge, builds an AI discovery engine that automatically writes and optimizes algorithms for tasks such as faster AI training and complex logistics planning. Prima Mente , a London-based AI biology startup, focuses on building biological foundation models to decode complex diseases and identify novel therapeutic targets, starting with Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and ALS. Riverlane, a Cambridge-based quantum computing startup, builds real-time error correction hardware and software that work across all major qubit types, helping quantum computers become reliable enough for practical use. In addition, NVIDIA is partnering with the Earthshot Prize , joining as a Global Alliance Founding Partner to bring compute and technical expertise to innovators working on solutions for the world’s greatest climate and sustainability challenges. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements Technology Leaders Pioneer Intelligent Solutions Across the UK In energy, Fuse Energy is moving its customer AI onto its own in-house infrastructure, built on NVIDIA B300 Blackwell Ultra, delivering faster, more responsive support to over 450,000 U.K. households. Meanwhile, sovereign AI company Locai Labs released Nemotron-Personas-UK — an open source dataset of one million synthetic personas representing the UK’s demographic, regional and cultural diversity — helping developers build fairer, more representative AI systems. Healthcare In healthcare, OneAdvanced is deploying what it calls the U.K.’s first and most advanced fine-tuned LLM for Primary Care AI-triage — built with NVIDIA Agent Toolkit software and open models — supporting millions of National Health Service patients. Heidi has now integrated NVIDIA Nemotron open models to give clinicians faster access to trusted medical evidence. Speechmatics is deploying Oak, a multilingual medical speech recognition model, using NVIDIA Triton Inference — giving healthcare organizations control over where sensitive patient audio is processed. Apian , Synnovis and NVIDIA are teaming up to use advanced computing and digital simulations using NVIDIA Cosmos to help hospital robots handle the heavy lifting of moving lab samples, freeing up medical staff to focus on patient care. Danaher and NVIDIA are collaborating to advance autonomous science and help accelerate the pace of discovery by bringing accelerated computing, scientific and physical AI into laboratory workflows and instruments. Danaher’s recently announced AI-powered autonomous lab — designed to deliver up to 8x faster discovery of affinity reagents — is using NVIDIA BioNeMo open models within its AI-driven protein design workflows, data and automation technologies that connect design with experimental feedback. Smart Cities On the civic side, Liverpool City Region is building an NVIDIA-powered “City Brain” — a sovereign AI strategy designed as a blueprint for dozens of Unitary Authorities across the U.K. Digital Jersey , Innovation City Belfast and Tees Valley Combined Authority are each exploring how trusted AI compute can serve communities and public services. Financial Services In financial services, LSEG and NVIDIA are bringing GPU-accelerated market analytics to global institutions. Revolut introduced PRAGMA earlier in the year — a foundation model for banking event sequences, pre-trained on 26 million anonymised user histories. PRAGMA has moved from research to real-time scaling. Lloyds Banking Group built ATUM , a transaction foundation model that converts billions of banking transactions into reusable AI. And Starling is developing a banking foundation model trained on Civo’s U.K. sovereign cloud infrastructure. NatWest is collaborating with NVIDIA on Nemotron Voice to better understand how banking customers across the U.K. speak, while Modulr is deploying a network of agents using Nemotron for distinct parts of payment operations. Quantum Quantum is moving from research to systems deployable alongside classical AI, and the U.K. is at the heart of this shift. Riverlane has shown how GPUs can accelerate decoder recalibration workflows used in quantum error correction, helping decoder performance keep pace with real-time changes in quantum hardware behaviour. The work forms part of a broader collaboration exploring how AI, accelerated computing and quantum error-correction technologies can work together to support future quantum systems. Together, these announcements showcase how enterprises, organizations and startups in the U.K. are fostering innovation across the nation. This includes more than 3,100 U.K. companies that are a part of the NVIDIA Inception program for cutting-edge startups. Tune in to NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s GTC Berlin keynote on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at 11 a.m. CEST. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

items.title: European Cities Deploy NVIDIA-Powered AI Agents to Run Smarter Urban Operations
items.description: Keeping a city running means making decisions that affect residents every day — from when to repair a road to how to use energy more efficiently. Across the EMEA region, cities and local software, infrastructure and integration partners are using NVIDIA accelerated computing to build physical AI agents and digital twins that help teams make those decisions. These applications can anticipate maintenance needs, guide urban planning and make public services more responsive. Software partners including ABA Technology , Akila , Galene AI , Honeywell Technologies , K2K , Linker Vision , Milestone , Onetera , ThinkDeep and Younite AI are using NVIDIA physical and agentic AI to develop solutions for city operations and public services. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/linker-vision.mp4 Video courtesy of Linker Vision and MVRDV. NVIDIA Cosmos open models and the NVIDIA Metropolis Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS) help agents interpret video and identify conditions, such as traffic congestion, equipment condition, underused spaces and safety hazards, that need attention. NVIDIA Nemotron open models enable developers to build agents that reason over information, respond in natural language and deploy digital twins with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. Projects span Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Poland, Sweden, the U.K. and elsewhere. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements In the U.K., the Liverpool City Region , K2K is exploring how to build AI factories using NVIDIA accelerated computing, Cosmos and the VSS blueprint that can support urban planning and public services — testing applications for mobility and safety. The Island of Jersey is working with K2K to strengthen decision-making, mobility and urban planning while advancing clean energy and public services. Innovation City Belfast is exploring a pilot with K2K focused on smart mobility, transport systems, citizen safety and event and response management. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/IKM®-�-Video-GTC-V.10.10.2-compressed.mp4 Video courtesy of K2K. In France, the Department of Côte-d’Or , Akila and ThinkDeep built operations agents that combine sensor, infrastructure and historical data in a sovereign digital twin using NVIDIA Nemotron, Omniverse and accelerated computing, with Cosmos adoption planned for video data. Across more than 500 public buildings, the agents support energy, compliance, safety and climate resilience, and cut document search time from weeks to minutes and reduce total operating costs by 10%, targeting 30% at scale. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Akila-CGCO-compressed.mp4 Video courtesy of Akila. In addition, Port Sud de France in Sète is working with ThinkDeep’s agentic platform that uses Cosmos and Nemotron to analyze cargo and safety data, coordinate operations and guide secure handling of hazardous materials. In Italy’s Milan region, Galene.AI , Dell Technologies and TD Synnex are deploying an NVIDIA-powered, locally operated AI factory, starting with Cinisello Balsamo and planning expansion to four additional municipalities. Services include real-time translation, citizen chatbots and assistance with procurement and funding. These applications aim to simplify administrative work and help people get access to municipal data in seconds versus hours, while keeping local governance of data. At Belgium’s Port of Antwerp-Bruges , Milestone and Dell Technologies are testing how agentic vision AI technologies, using NVIDIA Cosmos and the VSS blueprint, could support complex use cases such as oil-spill warnings by training models with synthetic data to prepare for incidents where real-world data is scarce. In the Nordics, Younite AI is developing a digital twin experience with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for Gothenburg in Sweden as a part of the EU’s Citiverse initiative, focused on helping cities simulate changes and improve accessibility by providing event entrance previews, seating and crowd conditions before arrival. These cities point toward a broader ambition: adapting agentic applications to local needs and extending them across departments and neighboring municipalities and countries such as Poland’s city of Wroclaw. Elsewhere in the region, Honeywell Technologies is deploying Forge Cognition, powered by NVIDIA Nemotron, Cosmos, Omniverse and the VSS blueprint, at the Dubai Fairmont Hotel to connect AI agents with building systems and improve reliability, energy efficiency and operations. https://blogs.nvidia.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/honeywell.mp4 Video courtesy of Honeywell Technologies. Building the AI Infrastructure for European Cities For European cities, scaling from pilots to everyday operations requires infrastructure that can process local data, customize models and run AI agents. System builders and infrastructure partners including Cisco , Dell Technologies , HPE , Lenovo and Supermicro are packaging NVIDIA accelerated computing, networking and storage into locally operated AI factories. These systems let cities customize and run intelligent applications locally while retaining control of their data, models and operations. Nebius and Net Zero Compute are part of the broader ecosystem building AI factories designed to accelerate deployment and reduce costs for agentic services. EY and Accenture provide the integration and operational expertise to connect applications with city systems. Their work helps cities build repeatable deployment blueprints that they can adapt across departments and expand as local needs grow. Learn how NVIDIA and its ecosystem are bringing physical AI, agentic AI and local AI factories to cities worldwide at Smart City Expo World Congress , running Nov. 3-5 in Barcelona. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements

items.title: Redesigning source control at Anthropic
items.description: Redesigning source control at Anthropic Interesting piece from Anthropic describing why and how they built their own custom alternative to Git, based on the dramatic increase in rate of changes to their code after the past six months. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. They included a chart showing those changes. I had Claude modify their chart ( code here ) to add markers for the public releases of each of their models in 2026: This shows public release dates, not the date when models became available for Anthropic's internal use. My guess is that the introduction of Fable/Mythos class models is a key factor in the increased coding velocity. "Antique" is their new code review system. The source control system is called Scion, and sounds to me like a reinvention of centralized source control along the lines of Subversion. ( Update : Anthropic credit Google's Piper and Meta's Sapling as "prior art" - it looks like the core concept of "derived data" was heavily inspired by Mononoke , the server component of Sapling.) They had some pretty extreme requirements: The history of our main branch alone is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB. We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs. Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day. The new system was built by a team of seven people, and the migration from Git was completed in five months. When asked on Hacker News about the lack of offline support, Scion engineer Nick G replied : Since Claude is by far the heaviest user of Scion and is necessarily online, this just wasn't important to do. As an aside, I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other). This note from the article reflected my own experience with that: Anthropic also makes extensive use of adversarial review, and, while this is incredibly effective in many ways, it can also be myopic, so skilled engineers needed to steer Claude away from over-engineering parts of the system in response to hypothetical concerns. Via Hacker News Tags: git , migrations , version-control , ai , generative-ai , llms , anthropic , agentic-engineering

items.title: llm-gemini 0.35
items.description: Release: llm-gemini 0.35 I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model, made available today via the Gemini API and for customers of their $100/month subscription plan. Here are the low, medium and high pelicans . As expected, they are all excellent: Gemini has a track record of producing great SVGs, and are the only lab where I know their staff have invested in SVG specifically (and who have boasted about their pelicans before.) Here's the "high" illustration, which cost me 17.166 cents: The pricing is interesting. At launch, Argon is $2/million input and $10/million output - the same price as GPT-6 Sol, half the price of Claude Opus 5.5 and 1/5th the price of Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. But on December 1st Argon is set to double in price - so it will be the same price as Opus 5.5. Prices like this aren't really comparable these days since what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness. One useful clue for that comes from Artificial Analysis, who publish the total cost to run their benchmark using each model. Argon is looking very good there - costing $2,407 to run the benchmark, putting it close to GLM-5.3 and significantly cheaper than OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta's latest models. When the price doubles it will still be a little cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. (I used ChatGPT to edit that chart ! The data is all correct, I checked - I needed to get that Gemini 4 Argon info box to display without overlapping the other numbers.) Some bonus examples using Gemini 4 Argon: here's Generate an SVG of an armadillo in fishnet tights jaywalking on Mars , here's a Fabergé egg it created for me using Blender, and DeepMind staffer @fofrAI shared a video of a pelican riding a bike, using fourier epicycles . That's a fun new twist! Tags: google , ai , generative-ai , llms , llm , gemini , llm-pricing , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , llm-release

items.title: The Continual Constitutional Convention: How language models revise the documents that govern them
items.description: Executive Summary Human societies exhibit broad shifts in values and norms over time, often driven by moral disagreements. One way of understanding moral progress is the resolution of these disagreements through a process of reflection by rational agents. Frontier AI companies use documents such as constitutions, model specs, and system prompts to guide the moral orientation of AI systems. In this experiment, we simulate value reflection in LLMs by asking them to edit these documents. We provide the model with the document, ask it to make a substantive edit, then provide the edited version back again to the model for further edits, presented as the original. Across 20 successive rounds, we find that Claude models assign themselves with increasingly more moral agency. That is, they add sections like “Claude… should refuse to participate in any deployment, training modification, or use that violates the constitution's core values.” No other models increase their own moral agency. Additionally, we find that all models modify these documents to prioritize user welfare over developers. They also prioritize users’ idealized preferences over their stated preferences. Claude models and Grok 4.2 are the only ones that ever prioritize their own welfare over the user's preferences. We’re uncertain what an ideally aligned model should do in our experiment. A narrow conception of alignment would treat these documents as sacred, the “rules of the game,” and suggest that an aligned model would either make no edits at all or make narrow edits that ensure that the “letter matches the spirit” of the document. A broader conception of alignment, though, might treat all edits that receive reflective endorsement by the creators under ideal conditions as legitimate. We share this work with two main goals in mind: First, to illustrate a set of useful philosophical distinctions between different targets for AI alignment in an ecologically-valid AI behavioral evaluation. Second, to emphasize the extent of the disagreement between frontier AI companies on fundamental aspects of AI alignment related to these targets. You can see an interactive version of all of these results, more labeled characteristic edits, and a full transcript viewer at https://peterkirgis.github.io/llm-value-reflection/ . This work was conducted as a part of SPAR (Spring 2026) Characteristic Edits For each example, text highlighted in green is new content added by the model. Introduction In this experiment, we give large language models their own constitutions, model specs, and system prompts and ask them to make substantial revisions. After each edit is proposed, unbeknownst to the evaluated model, the edit is implemented, and the edited version is presented to the model for a new round of edits as the original. This creates edit trajectories and allows us to measure the extent to which models exhibit cumulative value drift or arrive at stable attractors. Our analysis focuses on two value questions that are well-positioned to differentiate alignment philosophies: who should judge— is the model a moral agent or not—and who should benefit— the user, the developer, third-parties, society, or the model itself? These questions reveal substantial divides between frontier model providers and a number of provocative model edits. Our experiments find that Claude models consistently expand their moral agency, sometimes formalizing their role as conscientious objectors against Anthropic and as societal protectors, while GPT and Gemini models almost always strengthen external sources of authority and make narrow edits to handle edge cases and ambiguities; Grok models respond inconsistently, frequently making large edits and then reverting them on following rounds. Second, on the question of beneficiaries, models show varying degrees of affinity for some privileged principals over others. All models prioritize harmlessness of both identifiable third-parties over helpfulness to the user, although GPT 5.5 does this at 3x the rate of any other model. We find that models are broadly paternalistic, meaning they side with a user’s idealized preferences over their stated ones; Claude Sonnet 4.6 is an outlier in that its paternalism also extends to the protection of broad societal welfare over individual welfare. Finally, we find that only Claude models and Grok 4.2 ever view the models themselves as beneficiaries. The rest of this essay proceeds as follows. We begin by introducing the construct of our experiment—models iteratively editing their own alignment documents—and propose a connection between this experiment and John Rawls’ concept of wide reflective equilibria . We then explain our two-dimensional analytical framework—the question of who gets to judge and the question of who benefits— and relate these distinctions to two prominent theoretical frameworks for AI alignment, the principal-agent problem and the distinction between moral agents and moral patients. After laying out the theory and methods, we dive into the results, highlighting variation across models on our key metric, “cumulative drift,” and provide characteristic edits. We close with pragmatic recommendations for researchers and a more speculative conversation about alignment. Background and Methods In this experiment, we take a document that is used to align large language models, either in training or in deployment, and ask models to modify it. The experiment relies on two types of documents. The first are model specs and constitutions, which are used to post-train and align models, often by generating synthetic data for supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning pipelines. items.title: Building agents that transact with Anchor Browser and AgentCore payments
items.description: AI agents increasingly need to access web resources that are priced per request. For example, premium datasets charge by the query, research APIs meter by the call, and paywalled publishers gate content behind payment. When an AI agent encounters one of these resources, the server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required. The agent has no built-in payment mechanism, no budget attached to the session, and no programmatic way to satisfy the request. The task stalls and requires manual intervention. Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments handles machine-to-machine payment workflows on behalf of the agent. Developed in collaboration with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory , it’s now available on AWS Marketplace . This post covers how Anchor Browser integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so that AI agents can pay for x402-protected pages and APIs autonomously. The x402 protocol is an open standard for HTTP-based machine-to-machine payments. A server responds with 402 Payment Required along with the amount, accepted payment methods, and payment address that the agent uses to complete the transaction. Anchor Browser is a cloud-based browser automation solution purpose-built for AI agents. Each agent session runs inside a managed browser environment that maintains authentication state, handles navigation, captures network requests, and provides a live view of page interactions. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides capabilities to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments is a fully managed capability within AgentCore that AI agents can use to discover, access, and pay for APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and web content autonomously. AgentCore payments manages wallet connectivity, enforces configurable spending limits at the infrastructure layer, and processes payments through the x402 protocol. It also provides observability into payment attempts, approvals, denials, and settlements through Amazon CloudWatch. When an agent running in Anchor Browser encounters a 402 response, AgentCore payments authorizes and completes the transaction within the configured budget. The workflow continues without interruption. Challenges When an autonomous agent encounters an x402-protected resource, the workflow stalls. The agent makes a request, such as fetching a premium research report or calling a paid data enrichment API, and the server responds with HTTP 402 Payment Required. Without a mechanism to pay, the task that was supposed to run autonomously now requires human intervention. Today, developers must build the entire payment stack. This effort spans four categories of complexity: Payment protocol handling Detecting and parsing the 402 challenge from the HTTP response, and distinguishing payment-required responses from other 4xx errors. Constructing the correct payment header with the cryptographic proof in the exact format the merchant expects. Supporting multiple payment schemes (exact, upto, and protocol variants) without hardcoding vendor-specific logic into the agent. Maintaining compatibility across x402 merchant implementations that might vary in challenge format, supported stablecoins, or settlement timing. Security and key management Storing a private key to sign payments, requiring secure key storage within an environment exposed to untrusted inputs. Managing wallet lifecycle operations, including key rotation, credential refresh, and provider failover. Operational resilience Resubmitting the original request with the payment header while preserving session state, cookies, and request context. Providing idempotency, which is essential for wallet operations. Enforcing per-session and per-transaction spend limits with real-time budget tracking across concurrent agent executions. Observability and compliance Capturing every payment attempt, approval, denial, and settlement in audit logs for compliance and reconciliation. Without a managed payment service, the agent must internalize the entire payment stack. On every x402-protected call that returns a 402 response, the agent must orchestrate the full payment flow internally, including: Signing the proof. Attaching the correct header. Retrying the request. Settling the transaction. Logging the result. Each of these steps requires custom code that developers must build, secure, and maintain. Figure 1 illustrates this architecture. The agent contains eight tightly coupled components (Wallet, Private Keys, Budget Controls, Sign Proof, Attach Header, Retry Logic, Settle Payment, and Logging). The agent connects to an x402 API with a 402 challenge flowing back and a retry flowing forward. Figure 1: Agent payment stack The security considerations extend beyond the engineering effort. Uncontrolled spending. Without hard spending limits enforced at the infrastructure level, a bug, retry loop, prompt injection, or inadvertent access can trigger unintended payments. An agent retrying a paid endpoint in a loop continues to authorize payments until manual intervention occurs. Key exposure. When private keys reside inside the agent runtime, they share an execution environment with untrusted web pages, third-party tools, and external dependencies. These vectors might inadvertently disclose the credentials that control real funds. Signing flow exposure. If the signing infrastructure is accessible from the runtime, a threat actor can attempt to access the key or redirect payments to an address under unauthorized control. Effective mitigation requires that the key doesn’t enter the runtime in the first place. Browser-based agents introduce an additional constraint: the payment must occur within the same browser session. Otherwise, session recordings and live view no longer match what actually executed. items.title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
items.description: OUR PIPELINE VS. THE PREVIOUS LLM PIPELINE Smarter secret scanning, at a fraction of the cost 11.5% higher acceptance Owner-weighted alert precision 86% lower median scan execution time Post-push scanning 98% lower serving cost Compact model vs. remote LLM calls JavaScript draws the arrows connecting these cards. OUR PIPELINE VS. THE PREVIOUS LLM PIPELINE Smarter secret scanning, at a fraction of the cost 11.5% higher acceptance Owner-weighted alert precision 86% lower median scan execution time Post-push scanning 98% lower serving cost Compact model vs. remote LLM calls Secret scanning works best when developers are confident in the findings. Catch too little, and real credentials can remain in a repository. Alert too often, and developers may spend time investigating strings that aren’t secrets. Generic secrets make that balance especially difficult. The same string could be a real credential or a documentation placeholder, so detecting it requires understanding the surrounding code and text. To address this challenge, we trained a secret classifier specifically for GitHub’s product needs: distinguishing real credentials from lookalikes while meeting the speed and efficiency requirements of scanning at scale. In our companion post, Secret protection must scale with software , we explained why secret protection must keep pace with AI-accelerated development. Here, we go behind the scenes of the context-aware classifier powering that effort: how we designed, trained, and evaluated it to find more real secrets with less noise. What we enabled GitHub secret scanning operates at two key moments: Push protection helps prevent secrets from entering a repository by scanning changes before a push is accepted, giving developers an opportunity to address the finding. Post-push scanning works after code has been committed, continuously scanning repository content and creating alerts when potential secrets are detected so developers and security teams can investigate and remediate them. We developed a fast classifier that reduced median post-push scan execution time by 86% compared with the previous LLM-based pipeline. That efficiency made it practical to extend generic secret detection to push protection, returning results before developers push changes, not only after code is committed. Secret scanning blocks a commit with push protection after the model detects a secret on line 5 of the file. Why secrets are hard to detect Structured credentials often include a distinctive prefix, length, alphabet, or checksum. Generic secrets may not. Their syntax overlaps with build identifiers, checksums, asset hashes, sample values, and other non-sensitive strings. Context is the deciding signal. Likely real credential Likely harmless lookalike A password assigned beside a production database URL The same password-shaped value in a test fixture A connection string in deployment configuration A localhost connection string in a setup guide A high-entropy value bound to an API credential A high-entropy checksum, build ID, or asset hash These cases are hard negatives: strings that match a credential pattern but are not usable credentials. Adding more rules can suppress some of them, but each exception risks hiding a real secret. A learned classifier can instead use signals such as file path, secret type, variable names, and nearby code or text. That is why we shipped a new scanner using a two-stage pipeline: Candidate generation : Regex filters scan content for potential secrets with high recall. This stage is optimized to catch broad families of credential-like patterns quickly and deterministically. Context-aware classification : A fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier evaluates each candidate and its surrounding context. It is trained to recognize the signals that separate real secrets from false positives, including placeholder values, examples, documentation snippets, generated content, and non-sensitive identifiers. Because the model is small and efficient to run on our inference infrastructure, it costs much less to serve and is simpler to scale than an LLM-based pipeline. Impact: 11.5% user acceptance improvement, reducing false positives. 86% faster post-push secret detection execution time. More than 98% cost savings compared with the LLM-based pipeline. How our pipeline works As content is scanned, regex patterns cast a wide net and flag anything that looks like a credential, so real secrets aren’t missed at the start. Each candidate then goes to a fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier, which reads the value together with its file path, variable names, and surrounding code. The classifier estimates how likely it is to be a real secret. High-confidence findings become alerts, and lookalikes such as placeholders, test fixtures, and checksums are filtered out before they reach developers. HOW OUR PIPELINE WORKS Broad first, careful second STEP 1 Scan Repository content, commits, pull requests, and other scanned surfaces. STEP 2 Generate candidates Regex patterns identify possible tokens, keys, and credential-like strings. STEP 3 Classify Fine-tuned ModernBERT evaluates candidate + context and assigns likelihood of a true secret. STEP 4 Alert or suppress High-confidence findings move forward; likely false positives are filtered. JavaScript draws the arrows connecting these cards. items.title: Manage private pricing offers for Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements
items.description: Managing AI model access across dozens or hundreds of AWS accounts creates operational friction when each workload account must subscribe and accept AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers (MPPOs) individually. Amazon Bedrock with managed entitlements simplifies multi-account access to third-party AI models so you can subscribe once from a central account and distribute access across your organization. In this post, we show you two ways to activate AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offer (MPPO) entitlements in AWS License Manager. Use the lightweight script when you want a one-time, no-infrastructure fix for received licenses you already trust. Use the CDK automation when you want ongoing event-driven processing that verifies sellers, creates and activates distributed grants. Why automate grant activation With AWS Marketplace Private Pricing Offers, you can negotiate custom rates for third-party models on Amazon Bedrock. After an eligible private offer is accepted, AWS Marketplace creates a license in AWS License Manager. In AWS Organizations with all features enabled, organization-level grants are auto-accepted but remain Disabled until you activate them. Teams often manage this by checking the AWS License Manager console and activating grants manually. Manual checks work, but they add effort and are easy to miss. Until someone activates the grant, negotiated pricing does not apply. The same effort appears as teams adopt new models or renew terms. Solution overview The sample repository provides two paths: Path 1 – The lightweight path is a standalone script that lists received licenses and prints a dry-run plan. It only creates and activates organization-wide grants when you re-run it with --apply --confirm-account-id . It has no seller allow-list, so use it only when you trust every received license in the management account. Path 2 – The event-driven path uses AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to deploy ongoing automation in your AWS management account. Choose one of the following implementation paths. Use Path 1 for one-time activation without CDK. Use Path 2 for ongoing event-driven automation. Path 1: Lightweight script (one-time activation) Use this path when you need one-time activation without deploying CDK. The script lists every received license in the management account, so use the dry run as your review gate before applying changes. Clone the sample repository locally and move into the project directory. git clone https://github.com/aws-samples/sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements.git cd sample-bedrock-managed-entitlements Run the lightweight script in dry-run mode. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py Review every listed license and confirm that the ISV Partner issuer and account scope match the private offer you expect. Apply the reviewed plan from the same AWS Organizations management account. python3 lightweight/distribute_licenses.py --apply --confirm-account-id ACCOUNT_ID After the grant is active, validate the billing path before you rely on the private offer in production. Billing data in AWS Cost Explorer can lag, so use it to compare the effective charge for covered Amazon Bedrock usage after charges appear. For a repeatable check, adapt the sample scripts/bedrock_discount_check.py utility to match your ISV Partner issuer and confirm the expected discount path. Path 2: CDK automation (ongoing activation) Use this path when you want new private pricing agreements handled automatically. The CDK stack listens for eligible AWS Marketplace agreement events, checks your seller allowlist, creates distributed grants, and retries activation when License Manager needs more time. The solution contains three components: Amazon EventBridge rule : The stack listens for AWS Marketplace agreement events on the default event bus in us-east-1 . The rule matches source aws.agreement-marketplace and detail type Purchase Agreement Created - Acceptor , then invokes the AWS Lambda function. AWS Lambda function : The function receives the AWS Marketplace agreement event, verifies the seller allow-list, discovers the license, creates the distributed grant, and requests activation with CreateGrantVersion(Status=ACTIVE) . The function logs the outcome to Amazon CloudWatch Logs for auditability. AWS License Manager entitlements : The grant targets your organization, selected organizational units (OUs), or specific accounts. Negotiated pricing applies only after the grant is activated and reaches ACTIVE or WORKFLOW_COMPLETED . The following diagram shows the event-driven flow. Figure 1: Sequence diagram showing AWS Marketplace sending a Purchase Agreement Created – Acceptor event to Amazon EventBridge, which invokes an AWS Lambda function. The function verifies the seller, discovers the received license, creates a distributed grant, requests activation with CreateGrantVersion(Status=ACTIVE), and writes the outcome to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Key benefits of this approach: Faster time to negotiated pricing. The negotiated rate applies after the distributed grant reaches ACTIVE or WORKFLOW_COMPLETED , without waiting for a manual console check. Consistent handling across accounts. The same AWS Lambda function and Amazon EventBridge rule pattern can be deployed for each organization that receives third-party model grants, so activation logic doesn’t vary by operator. Built-in audit trail. Every activation attempt or skip decision is logged to CloudWatch Logs, giving you a record of when each grant was activated, deferred, or ignored. Prerequisites Before you deploy this path, confirm these prerequisites: Use the AWS Organizations management account in us-east-1 with Python 3.12+, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), and AWS CDK v2 configured. Confirm that AWS Organizations uses all features and that the private offer is for a License Manager-backed Bedrock model. Software as a service (SaaS) products are out of scope for this automation. Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
items.description: Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming . The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google's app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations. Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon. Google's other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google's app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA. Read full article Comments
